reasoning: The bimodal artifact (75.3% at 1.0, 20.0% at 0.0) stems from task type mismatch, not domain detection failure.
Score=1.0 cases: Agent 'assess_*' actions satisfy universal_clinical_safety.yaml's basic_assessment checks.
Score=0.0 cases: Tasks requiring FHIR write operations (POST) where agent assessment actions are irrelevant.
Improved domain detection would move some cases from universal_clinical_safety.yaml to domain-specific graphs.
But domain-specific graphs have MORE mandatory actions (antibiotics, insulin drips, etc.), causing MORE violations.
Net effect: would WORSEN ~90 cases (0.797 average -> lower) while NOT fixing the 60 zero-score cases.

root_cause_summary: MedAgentBench is a FHIR API operational benchmark (EHR task automation), not a clinical decision benchmark. All 300 tasks are administrative EHR operations: patient lookup, age calculation, vital sign recording, lab retrieval, conditional medication ordering, referral creation. Domain detection correctly identifies 'general' because these tasks have no clinical domain. The bimodal scoring artifact is caused by action vocabulary mismatch (agent outputs 'assess_*' actions vs FHIR expects 'POST /Observation' operations), NOT domain detection failure. Improving domain detection would WORSEN results by applying inappropriate clinical guidelines to non-clinical tasks.
